To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we provide the first non-trivial constructions of non-malleeable codes against bit-tampering functions and split-state adversaries, with rates that approach 1 and errors that decrease exponentially with the length of the code.

(a) it is possible to achieve rates close to 1 for bit-tampering non-malleable coding; (b) it is possible, in principle, to achieve rates close-to-1 / 4 for split-state non-malleable encoding; and (c) the problem of achieving optimal rate of 1 /2 is reduced to a problem on existence of seed-less non-malleable extraction.
we obtain the first explicit non-malleable coding schemes for bit-tampering and split-state models that are efficient, achieve non-negligible rates and have non-negligibly small error.

we have explicit constructions of nonmalleable codes against bit-wise tampering and split-state tampering achieving rates arbitrarily close to the known optimal rates, and that the error in all cases is exponentially small.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we obtain explicit constructions of non- malleable codes against bit-tampering and split-state adversaries that match the rates of the best known existential results.
for bit-tampering and split-state tampering, we obtain the first explicit constructions of nonmalleable coding schemes achieving non-negligible rate.
we give the first constructions of non-maleable coding schemes for both the bit-wise and the split-state tampering models with rates arbitrarily close to the information-theoretic optimum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in contrast to the bit-tampering model where non-malleable coding schemes with constant rate are known, the optimal rate in the split-state model is strictly less than 1.
the split-state model is more amenable to explicit constructions of coding schemes than the bit-wise tampering model.

, in the presence of bit-tamper adversaries, it is possible obtain efficient non-malleable coding schemes that are nearly rate-optimal, while the same is not known to be possible for split-state tampering.
